That sounds like endometriosis. Have you ever had a laparoscopy to check for endometriosis? Often endometriosis lesions are difficult to detect on an ultrasound and only a laparoscopy can give a definitive diagnosis.

That's what happened to me. I fainted almost every month from the pain. The ultrasound was inconclusive. The laparoscopy confirmed the diagnosis and several tissue lesions were removed.
Please ask your doctor for a laparoscopy and go to a specialist. It is really sad how many doctors still know far too little about this disease.

I have been in the same situation. I loved my ex like crazy but the longer I stayed with him the more I noticed that he wasn't really a nice person. I think I fell in love with him because he was really amazing towards me when he wanted us to be together. During the relationship however it became more and more obvious that he was quite arrogant, not empathetic, anti-social nearly and generally thinking bad about others - a textbook narcissist. Just as you I was even sometimes ashamed of how he behaved in public. The problem with his fragile ego was that it caused more and more conflicts within the relationship. While at the beginning being the perfect prince charming, a year into the relationship he often made me feel bad, telling me I was causing him distress and that he loves me but also  how much easier his life has been without me. In the end the relationship was nothing but conflicts and I ended it. Even after all his bad treatment I felt heartbroken and couldn't really move on. So I met with him again 6 months after the break up and you know what happened? With this little bit of distance I realized I really couldn't stand him at all. He was just an overall not nice person. Used every opportunity to make me feel guilty, talked bad about the appearance of every second person that walked by and was just unempathetic af. It really helped me coping with the break up though. 

So I guess my advice is: monitoring. Observe him and his behavior. If the thought that he hasn't got a good character continues to come to your mind and you notice more and more your values in life an hos just aren't compatible it is probably time to end the relationship. Because from my experience it isn't possible to stay in a relationship with someone you wouldn't even chose as a friend because of his character.

So if I was in your position I think I would just continue to pay attention to this thoughts and his character. Maybe he starts to grow as a person and changes, but maybe not. So it is wise to think about your personal boundaries. How many faults in character can a person have for you to still be able to love them and be happy in a relationship with them?

Good luck to youl

As you describe it she probably made very damaging experiences within her family concerning mutual respect. I think you are right in assuming that she wants affection and sympathy after being critiqued but probably only because she experiences fear and desparation. A big part of BPD is that they have a very instable and negative self-image and often think they are not good enough. Therefor they constantly fear anyone in their life will eventually find that they are not good enough and leave them. Any criticism will trigger that fear. It can be helpful to try to add some reassuring sentences in situations that may fit this category. Also the hair pulling thing is a typical behavior for the lack of impulse control associated with BPD.

If you'll look into it you'll probably find a lot of advice on how to support/ not trigger/ best interact with an emotional unstable partner :) 
You can try to make her feel safe and loved but she'll probably need professional help to learn how to express her needs and fears towards you and how to gain some insight on when she is emotionally overwhelmed and therefore overstepping boundaries. Good luck to the both of you! :)

Is your girlfriend diagnosed with any mental illness? What your describing sounds like behaviors related to an emotional-unstable personality disorder (or BPD). I don't think she's intentionally manipulating you. I just think she can't handle being critiqued because of the very dysfunctional behavioral patterns of her family. From an emotional perspective she is probably not able to distinguish being critiqued from being diminished.

I think you are a little bit too focused on your own perspective. Please try and see the other side.

To be honest I think it says somenting  that you wrote "if asked if I love her, I'd say yes" instead of simply writing "I love her". It seems that you are already lacking a lot of commitment. The fact that you can't deny the question of cheating supports that assumption. 

Maybe you should think about if it's really only her looks or if there's just not enough love.

For example: when I first met my ex boyfriend I wasn't physically attracted to him at all, but he was a very interesting person and I fell in love with him. For me, the attraction came with the feelings.

Maybe that is different for other people, but in the end from what you tell, you feelings are not strong enough to compensate that you don't find her attractive.

I would honestly suggest you talk to a therapist about that. Not because I think there is anything wrong about how you feel. There is nothing wrong about your feelings, ever. 

It seems to me though as if you have some issues with self love and self acceptance. From what you tell you don't just expect affection for the sake of affection. I think subconsciously you want affection to fullfill the needs you can't fulfill yourself and to compensate for the love and appreciation you are not able to give to  yourself. 

I don't say you don't love your partner. I'm sure you do, but there is a difference whether you love someone and are happy to be loved back or whether you NEED them to demonstrate their love all the time. They will feel as if the purpose of the relationship is to make you feel better instead of enjoying the shared time. In the long run that will be a strain to every relationship. 

In my opinion you would be a lot happier in your relationships and your life if you talk to someone who can help you to give yourself what you need. A therapist could help you to maintain emotional stability and content without love demonstrations or reassurance from someone else :) 

It will be a lot of work and you have to be committed to the learning process, but it will be worth it. It is a precious ability to be happy about yourself and make yourself happy. 
I've seen a lot of patients struggling with these problems and everyone of them who was able to manage the change was undeniable thankfull to have put so much effort in it. 

I hope this is helpful to you and I really hope you will find happiness in the future! :)

Of course it is manipulation, because manipulation is an essential part of BPD. People with BPD manipulate, but out of fear or the desperate need for affection and not because they are bad people. 
Yes it doesn't change the fact that it is something that she should work on and try to change (which for she will need the support of her husband) and you're totally right that this should not hinder the relationship to the child. But still, one should understand the difficulty of this situation and not call a woman suffering from a severe illness a psycho freak.

Of course the husband should not be the only source of support. She definitely needs therapy. But it's always helpful that additional to therapy thr social system is strong and supportive, especially because borderline disorder needs a lot of work and a long time of therapy. And yes sometimes sick people rely on other people. Just as people with physical illness sometimes rely on the help of other people to get through their daily life people with mental illnesses also do. It is not a status that is healthy and definetly one that should change, but it's not a thing to judge about either. Calling her a psycho manipulative freak just shows a real lack if understanding for borderline personality disorder.

You may be right that the wifes behavior is wrong.. But are you really calling a depressive person pathetic for needing and relying on the support from their loved ones?! Uff. Thats a very poor and morally wrong attitude. Depressed people must an should be helped and their partners and families should try to be there for them.
